title: Private POC: low-touch onboarding + canary-to-dedicated bridge
content:
Purpose: capture a compact, execution-focused plan for onboarding regulated customers into a private deployment POC that starts with a low-friction private control plane and a small private inference pool, validates SLA and data residency, and then uses a canary bridge to move traffic to a dedicated capacity profile if throughput or latency requirements demand it. This doc is meant for solutions engineering + infra + customer security review

Executive summary recommendation:
- Start with a private control plane in customer VPC (managed agent) and small dedicated GPU pool in the same region (single AZ), not full on-prem. Keeps risk low while satisfying initial compliance needs.
- Implement a canary routing bridge that lets a subset of traffic escalate from the private pool to our Dedicated capacity in the event of overload or performance regressions. Canary is enabled via route policy and a canary key in the API request.
- Use short-lived KMS keys and explicit logging hooks to satisfy audit requirements. Record token-level cost and per-request latency in the customer's logging sink for the POC period.

Why this pattern? tradeoffs and motivation
- Goal: minimize upfront customer ops friction and install time while preserving a path to stable, supported Dedicated throughput if POC scales.
- Alternatives considered that we rejected: full on-prem VM delivery (long lead, infra-heavy), pure hosted access (fails for highly regulated data residency), and immediate large dedicated reservations (expensive and slow to provision).

Topology options evaluated (quick sketches):
1) Private control plane + small local GPU pool (recommended starter)
   - Control plane runs as managed agent in customer VPC.
   - Inference nodes: 2x small GPU nodes (e.g., A10 or equivalent) in single AZ.
   - Egress: none by default; KMS for custody of keys. Audit logs forwarded to customer CloudWatch/Stackdriver.
   - Pros: fastest install, lowest infra ramp. Cons: no automatic high throughput scaling.

2) Private control plane + canary bridge to Redwood Dedicated
   - Same as 1, plus a routing proxy in control plane that can forward requests to Redwood Dedicated endpoints when canary flag present or local queue > threshold.
   - Add policy: fallback to Dedicated only for non-sensitive traffic or approved data types.
   - Pros: seamless scale path, reduced risk of POC failure. Cons: requires clear data-contract and legal sign-off for any forwarded traffic.

3) Private full-dedicated reservation (fast path for enterprise)
   - Customer contracts dedicated pool with reserved capacity in region; we provision GPUs in their cloud account or as reserved Redwood capacity with strict network boundaries.
   - Pros: predictable throughput and SLA. Cons: procurement/commitment friction, longer lead time.

Checklist for deciding initial starter topology with a particular customer:
- Data residency requirement: yes -> private control plane mandatory.
- Data sensitivity classification: PII/PHI? If high, require CanForwardPolicy document and legal sign-off for any outbound to Dedicated.
- Expected TPS and 99th p90 latency requirement -> if steady-state tokens/sec exceeds local pool capacity by >2x, plan for immediate bridge testing.
- Procurement timeline -> if customer cannot commit to reserved capacity in 30 days, use starter topology.

POC runbook (high level tasks and owner notes)
1) Pre-engagement (SE)
   - Send simplified architecture one-pager and security questionnaire to customer. Attach SE-3124 baseline.
   - Confirm cloud account role IDs, KMS details, and preferred logging sink.
2) Day 0 install (Infra + SE)
   - Deploy control plane agent into customer VPC using customer-provided CloudFormation/Terraform snippet. Validate agent checkin.
   - Provision 2 small GPU nodes and sidecar logs/metrics exporter.
   - Confirm KMS key rotation policy and that logs are flowing to customer's sink.
3) Day 1 functional validation (SE + Eng)
   - Smoke test model endpoints with small prompt sets. Capture latency distribution, KV cache behavior.
   - Run correctness prompts from eval deck and store golden outputs.
4) Canary bridge test (Eng + SE)
   - Configure route policy: 5% of traffic with canary header forwarded to Dedicated endpoint. Ensure data filtering applied to exclude sensitive payloads.
   - Observe metrics for 48 hours. Log discrepancies and cost deltas.
5) Escalation criteria and cutover plan
   - If sustained 95th percentile latency > SLA for 1 hour OR local CPU/GPU queue > 80% for 15 minutes, automatically increase canary weight to 50% and notify stakeholders.
   - Final cutover to Dedicated requires procurement approval and a 24-hour scheduled migration window.

Operational telemetry and SLOs to record during POC
- Per-request latency p50/p90/p99
- Token/sec throughput and token cost per request
- Cache hit ratio and effective tokens saved by prefix cache
- Error rates by error class (OOM, rate limit, 5xx)
- Audit log completeness: percentage of requests with full trace id and KMS envelope id

Security and compliance notes (quick)
- Data forwarding policy must be explicit. Create a simple policy doc that lists allowed data types for Dedicated forwarding and required redaction steps.
- Use short-lived credentials for the control plane agent and rotate every 24 hours during POC.
- Provide customer with a linkage table mapping request_id -> KMS envelope for every forwarded request.

Capacity and cost assumptions (starter pool)
- 2x small GPUs estimated at 40-80 rps for typical chat prompts depending on model size. Expect headroom for bursty traffic but not sustained high throughput.
- Dedicated cost example: X GPU-hours at negotiated rate; will reflect in cost telemetry attached to POC billing report.

Known risks and mitigations
- Legal risk: accidental forwarding of sensitive records. Mitigation: conservative default of not forwarding any dataset flagged as sensitive; manual whitelist only.
- Performance risk: KV cache cold start causing high latency. Mitigation: warm-up runs and a small persistent cache priming job.
- Observability gap: customer logging sink misconfigured. Mitigation: pre-check via automated smoke pipeline before canary activation.

Open questions before customer workshop
- Does customer accept a canary of non-production traffic only, or do they want production traffic included?
- Which models are acceptable to forward to Redwood Dedicated (open models only, or vendor models too)?
- Procurement window for Dedicated commitment if cutover needed within 60 days?

Appendix: short action items for next SE meeting
- Draft CanForwardPolicy template and circulate for legal review (owner: Riya).
- Create a minimal Terraform snippet that provisions control plane + router and publish as template in SE repo (owner: Marco).
- Build a short eval prompt set for latency/cost regression testing and add to Confluence (owner: Omar).

Notes to self: this doc is intentionally pragmatic - prioritize low friction and legal clarity. Expect iteration after first customer workshop.

End of doc.
